exposure: Surgical specialties: orthopedic or trauma, general surgery, burn, plastic surgery, cardiac surgery, neurosurgery, vascular surgery, gastroenterology, gynecologic oncology
Type of procedure (obstetric delivery vs surgery)
outcome: Presence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in peritoneal cavity
Presence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in female reproductive tract
Presence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in the surgical or delivery suite environment
Presence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA inside the masks of health care workers
cohort: 32 adult patients (20-88 years old) undergoing urgent surgery or obstetric delivery with positive RT-PCR nasal swab for SARS-CoV-2
finding: SARS-CoV-2 RNA was detected in a small proportion (6%) of patient and environmental samples, but not on the inner surface of healthcare worker masks.
mod_finding: While the study included patients undergoing cesarean deliveries, it primarily focused on the presence of SARS-CoV-2 RNA in various samples and did not report specific findings related to mode of delivery.
